original_statement_or_assumption: Actuator sized from inertia + flexure + lateral drag mu*N = 0.15 N; sum 176 mN (N = 0.75 N, mu = 0.2)
finding: A laterally actuated nib must react the transverse component of the whole contact reaction, including the normal force: |R_perp| = N*sqrt((cos th + mu cos b sin th)^2 + (mu sin b)^2). The normal term N cos th was omitted and is quasi-static.
corrected_statement_or_value: At the report's own N = 0.75 N, mu = 0.2: mean |R_perp| = 0.62 N at 35 deg, 0.44 N at 55 deg, 0.22 N at 75 deg (4.2x, 3.0x, 1.5x the 0.15 N term). Bench corner (2 N, 35 deg, mu 0.35): 1.9 N.
evidence: analysis/audit_recalc.py (results/audit/audit_corrections.json, fig_transverse_load_vs_tilt.png); stabpen/contact.py; sim static test sim/tests/test_model.py::test_static_contact_load_matches_statics
consequence_for_design: Actuator force requirement is 3-10x higher and continuous; copper loss scales with F^2. Drives the lever/skid/bias configuration decisions (DEC-003, DEC-008).

report_section: s9 s22 Energy and thermal budget
original_statement_or_assumption: Runtime table assumes 8 ohm coils at 80-300 mA RMS with unspecified force constant; 0.15 N sustained needs ~1.9 N/A
finding: With COR-01 loads, holding power is (F/Km_tip)^2 independent of wire gauge. Direct drive with Km 0.15-0.6 N/sqrtW needs 1.2-19 W at the design point (1 N, 50 deg, mu 0.15).
corrected_statement_or_value: Direct drive near tip: ~12 W (Km 0.19 from field model) -> infeasible. Lever n=3.17 (Rev A): ~0.48 W contact copper loss (0.37 W writing average, ~96 min on 200 mAh). Skid + constant-force nib: ~0.07 W. Bias-actuator hybrid: ~0.02 W.
consequence_for_design: Onboard direct drive rejected; lever mandatory; product baseline candidates D (skid) and E (bias) carried forward.

original_statement_or_assumption: 0.5 mm transverse motion needs 0.71 mm axial accommodation at 35 deg
finding: Arithmetic correct for 0.5 mm TRANSVERSE motion (gives 0.87 mm page motion). The requirement is page-referenced.
corrected_statement_or_value: For a page disc of radius 0.5 mm: tilt-plane stage component 0.5 sin th, axial accommodation 0.5 cos th = 0.41 mm at 35 deg; lateral axis unchanged.
consequence_for_design: Axial travel sizing uses page-referenced values.

original_statement_or_assumption: Page gain = 1/sin(theta) along the tilt plane (J assumes axial motion freely accommodated)
finding: 1/sin(theta) holds only when the pen's axial suspension absorbs all tilt-coupled axial motion. If the suspension is stiffer than the hand normal compliance, the housing rises instead and the tilt-direction gain falls toward sin(theta).
corrected_statement_or_value: J_t1 = sin th + gamma cos^2 th / sin th with gamma = K_n sin^2 th / (K_n sin^2 th + k_ax). With k_ax = 2 kN/m and hand K_n = 800 N/m: gamma = 0.19 at 50 deg, J_t1 = 0.87 (vs 1.31). Uncompensated controller under-corrected tilt-direction motion by ~35% in simulation; compliance-aware J restored oracle ratio from 0.34 to 0.13.
evidence: sim/pensim/core.py (gamma_acc); diagnostic run (results/sim logs); derivation docs/physics.md eq. P-12
consequence_for_design: Controller must use a compliance-aware (identified) Jacobian; tilt-direction page workspace shrinks with a stiff axial path (stage needs ~0.6 mm for 0.5 mm page at 35-50 deg). gamma must be identified per user (EXP-B06).

original_statement_or_assumption: Passive axial compliance accommodates contact and tilt; soft compliance recommended implicitly
finding: A soft axial suspension converts writing-force variations into ink displacement along the tilt direction (dF/k * cos th) and produces pen-down hooks of ~1 mm (200 N/m); it bottoms out at modest loads.
corrected_statement_or_value: Device-induced ink distortion vs a rigid pen fell from 64 um RMS (200 N/m) to 22 um (>= 5 kN/m); pressure modulation under correction rose from 0.08 to 0.16 N RMS. Baseline set to ~2 kN/m axial path with force sensing, hand providing compliance.
evidence: simulation sweep (sim/pensim; command in docs/sim_report.md); results/sim
evidence_status: simulation (synthetic handwriting; unvalidated contact and hand models)
consequence_for_design: Stiff axial path with force sensor (DEC-006); pressure-modulation acceptability becomes an experiment (EXP-B08).

original_statement_or_assumption: 1 g moving assembly; undamped stage mode 35.6 Hz
finding: A refill + carrier + actuator part is 1.5-3 g in translation; a front-pivot lever has tip-equivalent inertia ~10 g (CAD Rev A). With a 50-150 N/m flexure the open-loop mode falls to ~11-19 Hz, inside the tremor band.
corrected_statement_or_value: Rev A CAD: moving parts 1.93 g, tip-equivalent mass 10.3 g (point-mass approximation); mode 19 Hz at 150 N/m.
consequence_for_design: Closed-loop position bandwidth >= 60 Hz with reference feedforward is required; flexure cannot set the dynamics.

original_statement_or_assumption: Residual |1-exp(-j w tau)| = 2|sin(pi f tau)| (e.g. 0.25 at 8 Hz, 5 ms)
finding: Correct only for unity-gain instantaneous actuation with exact amplitude. Closed-loop servo phase adds equivalent delay; a 60 Hz, zeta 0.7 servo adds ~3.7 ms at 8 Hz.
corrected_statement_or_value: Residual at 8 Hz: 0.25 (ideal 5 ms) -> 0.44 (5 ms + 60 Hz servo); 0.29 (2 ms + 60 Hz servo). Micron (verified primary source): 2 ms pure delay, 84-123 Hz bandwidth, 15 dB attenuation in free space.
consequence_for_design: Reference feedforward and prediction horizon must include servo lag; delay budget in docs/architecture.md.

original_statement_or_assumption: IMU: 1 mg bias gives 4.9 mm after 1 s
finding: Arithmetic correct but understates: a 0.1 deg attitude error leaks 1.7 mg of gravity (8.6 mm after 1 s); 70 ug/sqrtHz noise gives 0.4 mm random walk in 1 s. Over a 2 ms optical latency gap the IMU error is ~0.05 um.
corrected_statement_or_value: Conclusion strengthened; IMU used only to bridge optical latency and for orientation/contact events.
consequence_for_design: Estimator fuses IMU only over ms-scale gaps.

original_statement_or_assumption: Paired n ~ 32 for sigma_D = 2 delta (normal approximation)
finding: Exact two-sided paired t-test (alpha 0.05, power 0.8) needs n = 34 before attrition.
consequence_for_design: Sample-size planning uses t-based calculation and pilot variance.

report_section: s1 s4 s14 Scope and envelope
original_statement_or_assumption: Pen supports people with Parkinson's-related writing difficulties via local nib correction; +/-0.5 mm per axis
finding: Writing tremor that fits +/-0.5 mm: ~30% (plausible 15-50%) of drug-free ET patients have spiral tremor <= 1 mm p-p (Elble & Ellenbogen 2017, n=18, lead-verified; log-normal fit is our derivation). PD writing problems are dominated by micrographia (50-63% prevalence); tremor while writing uncommon (3/10 OFF-medication patients). No study gives writing tremor at the nib in mm.
corrected_statement_or_value: Active cancellation targets a subset of action/essential tremor; PD micrographia needs cueing/practice modes, not nib correction.
consequence_for_design: Separate user groups and claims; tremor-amplitude census at the nib is a decisive experiment (EXP-H01).

original_statement_or_assumption: Deterministic observer + optional causal model can cancel small unwanted movements while preserving intent
finding: Intended handwriting and tremor overlap spectrally. In simulation (synthetic lognormal handwriting, literature hand impedance, tuning seeds): best conventional estimator residual/neutral = 0.62 at 10 Hz, 0.76 at 8 Hz, 0.94 at 6 Hz, >1 at 4.5 Hz with 110-135 um intended-path distortion; band-pass cancellation worsens writing below 6 Hz. Mechanical (oracle) bound ~0.13-0.20.
corrected_statement_or_value: Estimation, not mechanics, limits benefit in free writing. Frequency-gated authority and known-path guidance required; held-out test results in docs/sim_report.md.
consequence_for_design: Adds frequency gate (per-user f_gate), guided mode emphasis, and a precise ML value proposition (EXP-E01).

original_statement_or_assumption: DRV8212 H-bridge + INA181 current amplifier
finding: DRV8212 has no integrated current sensing (datasheet 9.2.4). INA181 lacks enhanced PWM rejection (common mode -0.2..26 V, 350 kHz) and is a monitoring amplifier; inline sensing of an H-bridge-driven coil needs a PWM-rejecting amplifier.
corrected_statement_or_value: Use DRV8212 + inline shunt + INA241A (1.1 MHz, PWM rejection) or INA240 (93 dB AC CMRR at 50 kHz); or DRV8214 integrated IPROPI (+/-5%) inside a position loop.
consequence_for_design: Schematic uses INA241A inline per coil; sample timing tied to PWM centre.

original_statement_or_assumption: nRF5340 suitable baseline; sample analogue signals synchronously with drive
finding: nRF5340 has one multiplexed 12-bit SAR ADC (sequential sampling, 200 ksps), 16 MHz PWM clock (9.6 bit at 20 kHz edge-aligned), and Zephyr runs BLE host and control on the application core (network core has no FPU/DSP in that configuration).
corrected_statement_or_value: Current and Hall channels are sampled sequentially within a PWM-synchronised window (DPPI); a 50 kHz PWM gives ~8.3-bit resolution (dither required). Alternative STM32U5 for motor-control timers + dual ADCs.
consequence_for_design: Timing budget and ADC scan plan in docs/architecture.md; MCU decision DEC-010 keeps nRF5340 for research pen with STM32U5 fallback.

original_statement_or_assumption: 120 mAh cell for sensitivity; 'qualified protected single cell'
finding: Candidate small cylindrical cells have 1C limits (EEMB LIR10440: 320 mAh, 0.32 A max continuous), below actuator peak currents (~0.5-0.9 A).
corrected_statement_or_value: Use a high-rate narrow LiPo pouch (Grepow GRP5811047 200 mAh 20C, 5.6 x 11 x 47 mm; web-table claim to verify) or equivalent; add protection IC.
consequence_for_design: Battery envelope in CAD updated; cell qualification EXP-P01.

original_statement_or_assumption: Moticont 9.5 mm VCM (0.28 N cont.) as bench reference
finding: Its motor constant is only 0.21 N/sqrtW (Kf 0.29 N/A, R 1.9 ohm). A 12.7 mm VCM (LVCM-013-013-03: Kf 1.14 N/A, R 1.9 ohm, Km 0.83) is a better bench actuator.
corrected_statement_or_value: Bench rig uses 12.7 mm class VCMs through a lever.
consequence_for_design: Bench rig BOM updated.

original_statement_or_assumption: DeltaPen shows 1 kHz local optical tracking useful for correction
finding: DeltaPen (lead-checked row OPT-01/02): 1 kHz reports, translation error 68 um mean / 24 um median per 10 ms window, evaluated on a Wacom surface not paper, no latency figure, 10 x 12 mm tip board. P3040 datasheet NDA-gated; mouse sensors need 2.4 mm working distance.
corrected_statement_or_value: Optical sensing near a moving nib requires custom optics; noise per window is 5-20% of target tremor amplitude; latency unknown.
consequence_for_design: Optical path is a custom-optics risk with its own experiment (EXP-S01); research pen may use external reference first.

original_statement_or_assumption: Front zone holds nib, motion, compliance, sensing and optics; PCB alongside refill
finding: A 67 mm ISO D1 refill is longer than any lever that places the actuator in the grip, so the actuator must be annular around the swinging refill; optics near the nib conflict with nib motion; CAD mass 31.6 g before adhesives, wiring, fasteners and margin; CoM 81 mm from tip.
corrected_statement_or_value: Rev A layout in results/cad; mass margin ~3 g against 35 g target before allowances.
consequence_for_design: Mass and CoM are active constraints; lighter barrel material and cell choice under study.

original_statement_or_assumption: Crossed-leaf or nested planar stage deserves FEA
finding: Simple wire/rod pivots fail: stiff wires exceed fatigue stress (1.1 GPa at full travel), thin wires buckle under 2 N axial load (margin 0.4). Short-arm diaphragms exceed stress at a 1 mm stop.
corrected_statement_or_value: Cross-strip BeCu gimbal (0.05 x 1.0 x 2.0 mm blades): k_tip ~76 N/m, 177 MPa full travel, 82 MPa typical, buckling margin 19. Long spiral-arm diaphragms (15 mm, 0.22 mm) give ~2 kN/m axial at 230 MPa at a 0.6 mm stop.
consequence_for_design: Pivot = two-stage cross-strip gimbal; axial suspension behind pivot (constant lever arm).

original_statement_or_assumption: A passive neutral spring can move the tip on loss of power
finding: With a quasi-static transverse contact load N cos th, loss of actuator current drives the nib AWAY from centre toward the stop (the contact load exceeds the flexure force), drawing a mark of up to the stop travel.
corrected_statement_or_value: Controlled shutdown only at verified lift; brown-out hold-up energy for a ramped release; mechanical lock investigated.
consequence_for_design: Power-loss behaviour requirement REQ-SAF-004; firmware state machine.

original_statement_or_assumption: Strong continuous guidance may reduce learning; test unassisted
finding: Literature: error-removing channel assistance produced the worst unassisted retention and transfer in curve tracing (HAP-09); guidance improves fluency but not shape (HAP-10); benefit is skill-dependent (HAP-08).
corrected_statement_or_value: Assistance and training are separate modes; training mode uses fading, catch trials and error-amplification options.
consequence_for_design: Mode design and study endpoints revised.

original_statement_or_assumption: Small TCN 20k-200k params at 100-250 Hz feasible on nRF5340
finding: Dilated int8 convolutions run on CMSIS-NN's generic kernel; a published small TCN reached 0.15 MAC/cycle on Cortex-M4; ST Edge AI 4.0 does not support dilation != 1; whole-window recompute costs ~8 M MAC. Streaming implementation is mandatory.
corrected_statement_or_value: Budget: <= ~35k MAC per 4 ms step at 128 MHz; streaming ring buffers; TFLM + CMSIS-NN pinned commits.
consequence_for_design: ML deployment design in ml/deploy; MCU benchmark EXP-E02.

original_statement_or_assumption: Existing datasets useful for prototyping; ML Kit practical candidate
finding: IAM-OnDB/DeepWriting/MathWriting/BRUSH are non-commercial; ML Kit publishes no accuracy numbers and requires disclosure of metrics collection; MyScript developer terms do not permit distribution.
corrected_statement_or_value: A shipped recogniser needs a vendor licence or programme-owned data; evaluate ML Kit on our users first.
consequence_for_design: Recognition path decision DEC-013.

original_statement_or_assumption: >= 30% RMS path error reduction over a low-amplitude envelope as a gate
finding: Consumer digitising tablets have +/-0.25 mm accuracy (PDT-12 discussion) - larger than the effect; conventional estimators may not reach 30% below ~7 Hz in free writing (COR-11).
corrected_statement_or_value: Gate defined per frequency band and task type (known path vs free writing) with micrometre-class metrology and absolute error limits.
consequence_for_design: Gate G-B redefined.

original_statement_or_assumption: Hand impedance not quantified; reaction force noted qualitatively
finding: Measured stylus-grip impedance (Fu & Cavusoglu 2012, HAP-26): k1 380-770 N/m, b1 0.8-1.8 N s/m, M 0.2 kg, k2 79-272 N/m. A 30 g barrel on this grip resonates near 22 Hz with low damping; 0.1 N reactions move the barrel 0.1-0.2 mm; pen-hold vibrotactile threshold 26 um at 10 Hz (HAP-27).
corrected_statement_or_value: Hand model in simulation replaced by the measured two-stage model; reactions will be perceptible.
consequence_for_design: Simulation hand model v0.3; comfort evaluation in human studies.

original_statement_or_assumption: [7] 'Handwriting training in Parkinson's disease...' PLOS ONE, 2017, no authors listed
finding: Authors missing (Nackaerts E, Broeder S, Pereira MP, Swinnen SP, Vandenberghe W, Nieuwboer A, Heremans E). Year 2017 is correct (PLoS One 2017;12(12):e0190223); the development brief's R6 label '2018' is the discrepancy. R5 (Nackaerts 2016, Mov Disord 31(8):1209-1216) read at abstract level only.
corrected_statement_or_value: Nackaerts E et al. PLoS One 2017;12(12):e0190223. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0190223
consequence_for_design: None

original_statement_or_assumption: Contact load bench sweep 0.2-2 N; angle 35-75 deg; mu 0.2 for scale only
finding: Healthy adults: axial writing force mean 1.0 N (between-writer SD 0.43 N; writer means 0.56-2.08 N; within-word SD 0.18 N); normal ~0.8 x axial; heavy writers to ~4 N axial (derived high case). Altitude ~50 deg on paper (n=4) and 62 +/- 7.5 deg on tablets (95% range 47-77 deg). Ballpoint drag mu ~0.15 (0.09-0.4) with ~25% ripple along strokes (6-100 Hz disturbance). ISO 12757-1 writing test: 1.5 N at 75 deg, 4.5 m/min.
corrected_statement_or_value: Bench sweep 0.2-4 N; product assistance envelope proposed as N <= 1.2 N at theta >= 45 deg with graceful authority reduction beyond; 35 deg retained as a characterisation corner only.
evidence: CON-01, CON-02, CON-03, CON-12, CON-13, CON-14, CON-15, CON-21
evidence_status: literature (human studies, patents, standards via secondary text)
consequence_for_design: Worst-case loads come from heavy writers rather than extreme angles; skid/bias configurations (D/E) handle them without heat; friction ripple adds broadband disturbance for the servo.
affected_items: REQ-ACT-001; config writing.*; validation EXP-B01 EXP-B05

original_statement_or_assumption: US12026327B2 claim 1 includes actuated nib manipulator, IMU and character formation; EP4250070A1 related; CN121979402A describes movable refill and orthogonal linear drives
finding: US12026327B2 claim 1 (verbatim from USPTO text) recites nib motion along XP/YP AND a ZP axis, an IMU measuring the axis position relative to the writing surface, and scribing predefined characters from segment-formation commands; the description never mentions tremor. EP4250070A1 shown as Withdrawn (EPO search cited X documents US2020/0202741A1 and US4211012A). CN121979402A exists (pending): IMU plus eccentric-mass counter-moments, X-Y voice-coil/piezo drive of a refill guide ring with translation-only claim 7, camera, guided strokes. Verily US10101824B2 (active pen carriage redrawing tremor-filtered handwriting) and US11944216B2 require review. No claims found reciting predictive cancellation, confidence-based authority limiting or a pivoting refill.
corrected_statement_or_value: Feature-to-claims map and 17 attorney questions in docs/research/notes/PAT_patents.md; statuses as displayed on Google Patents, not verified in official registers.
consequence_for_design: Record independent design decisions; commission professional FTO review before production mechanism freeze; candidate differentiation: pivoting refill lever, compliance-aware Jacobian, confidence/frequency-gated authority.

original_statement_or_assumption: Deliberate rapid strokes and tremor can overlap in frequency (qualitative)
finding: Quantified: in a public online-handwriting recording (one writer, derived by the CON stream) ~17% of velocity energy lies in 4-7 Hz (0.2-0.3 mm RMS intended motion for 3-4 mm letters) and ~1.5% in 8-12 Hz; velocity spectrum flat to ~5 Hz, near noise by ~10 Hz (CON-24). Healthy older adults already place 36% of pen angular-velocity power in 4-7 Hz (CON-10).
corrected_statement_or_value: Independent support for the ~8 Hz separability boundary found in simulation (COR-11); frequency-gated authority justified.
consequence_for_design: Free-writing tremor cancellation targets >= ~8 Hz components; lower-frequency tremor handled by guided tasks, stabilisation strength trade-off and later learned context.
